name: security-fix-release
note: Fixture evidence for a fictional repository. Shows a released security fix.
evidence:
Repository: example-org/tinyvault
Status: Released
- advisory: "Path traversal in backup restore" severity=critical CVE-2099-0001 published 2099-01-10
- release v2.4.1 published 2099-01-10: "Fixes path traversal in the backup restore command (CVE-2099-0001). All users should upgrade."

explanation.headline: tinyvault releases version 2.4.1 to fix a critical backup security flaw
explanation.whatHappened: The maintainers of tinyvault published version 2.4.1. It fixes a security flaw in the command that restores backups.
explanation.previously: In earlier versions, a specially made backup file could write files outside the folder it was supposed to stay in.
explanation.whatChanged: Version 2.4.1 checks where each restored file will go and refuses paths that escape the backup folder.
explanation.whyItMatters: Anyone who restores backups they did not create could have had important files overwritten. The maintainers rated the flaw critical and ask all users to upgrade.
explanation.nextConfirmed: The advisory tells all users to upgrade to version 2.4.1.
explanation.nextSpeculative: Projects that bundle tinyvault might publish their own updates.

glossary.definition: A public notice that describes a security flaw and how to fix it.
A trick where a file name like ../../ makes a program reach folders it should not touch.
A public ID number given to a known security flaw so everyone can refer to the same problem.

explanation.analogy: It is like a mail room that delivered packages to any address written on the box, even rooms outside the building. Now it checks the address first.
explanation.intermediate: The restore command joined archive paths to the target folder without normalizing them. Version 2.4.1 rejects entries that resolve outside the target.
explanation.technical: Archive entry names containing ../ sequences were resolved relative to the restore root without canonicalization (CVE-2099-0001). The 2.4.1 release validates the resolved path prefix before writing.
